name: Artemis 3 (Amundsen)
desc: Proposed lunar south polar landing region near Amundsen crater. Offers access to ancient highland terrain and nearby permanently shadowed regions of scientific interest.

name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow)
desc: Final Apollo lunar landing site, situated in the Taurus-Littrow valley between mountainous highlands and volcanic mare terrain. Selected to investigate highland materials and volcanic deposits.

name: Apollo 11 (Mare Tranquillitatis)
desc: Historic first crewed lunar landing site, located within Mare Tranquillitatis. A relatively smooth mare basalt plain selected to demonstrate the feasibility of a crewed lunar landing.

name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)
desc: Located in the Fra Mauro highlands, containing material associated with the Imbrium impact basin. Selected to investigate lunar crustal materials and impact ejecta.

name: Apollo 15 (Hadley-Apennine)
desc: Located near Hadley Rille and the Apennine Mountains, providing access to mountainous highland terrain, volcanic plains and a prominent lunar geological rille.

name: Apollo 12 (Oceanus Procellarum)
desc: Located in Oceanus Procellarum (Ocean of Storms), a large lunar mare region. Selected to investigate mare basalt deposits and demonstrate precision landing capabilities.

name: Apollo 16 (Descartes Highlands)
desc: Located in the Descartes Highlands, an elevated lunar region investigated for ancient crustal materials and geological history, including highland rocks and impact-related deposits.

name: Artemis 3 (Faustini Rim A)
desc: Proposed lunar south polar landing region near the rim of Faustini crater. Offers access to polar highland terrain and proximity to permanently shadowed regions that may contain water ice.

name: Artemis 3 (Haworth)
desc: Proposed lunar south polar landing region associated with Haworth crater. Offers opportunities to investigate ancient highland terrain and potentially volatile-bearing permanently shadowed regions.

name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A)
desc: Intuitive Machines' first CLPS lander, which touched down near Malapert A crater in 2024. The first US landing since Apollo and the first commercial lander on the Moon.

name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
desc: Intuitive Machines' second CLPS lander, sent to the Mons Mouton region in 2025 to test drilling for ice near the south pole.

name: Blue Ghost M1 (Mare Crisium)
desc: Firefly Aerospace's first CLPS lander, which landed in Mare Crisium in 2025 and operated through a full lunar day.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram landing site)
desc: ISRO's Vikram lander and Pragyan rover, which landed in the high southern latitudes in 2023. India's first soft landing on the Moon.

name: SLIM (Shioli crater)
desc: JAXA's Smart Lander for Investigating Moon, which landed near Shioli crater in 2024 to demonstrate pinpoint landing.

name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán crater)
desc: CNSA's lander and Yutu-2 rover in Von Kármán crater, the first soft landing on the lunar far side (2019). Direct-to-Earth contact is impossible here; it relies on a relay satellite.

name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo basin)
desc: CNSA's far-side sample-return mission, which landed in the Apollo basin in 2024. Like Chang'e 4, it needs a relay satellite to talk to Earth.
